channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Turkey Pursues "Complete Revolution" in Defense Industry, Says Erdogan
item.description: President Recep Tayyip Erdogan announced Turkey is initiating a "complete revolution" in its defense industry, aiming to expand achievements and meet the defense needs of friendly nations upon request. He emphasized strengthening allies enhances Turkey's own strength.

item.title: Afghan Foreign Minister Meets UN Under-Secretary-General DiCarlo
item.description: Amir Khan Muttaqi, Afghanistan's acting Foreign Minister, and Rosemary DiCarlo, UN Under-Secretary-General for Political and Peacebuilding Affairs, discussed cooperation, humanitarian aid, and the needs of returning migrants. Both sides emphasized ongoing collaboration.

item.title: Russia Strikes Military Equipment Storage Center in Kyiv
item.description: Russia's Defense Ministry announced its forces attacked the Gostomel logistics center in Kyiv, where equipment for the Ukrainian armed forces was stored. This strike occurs amid intensified reciprocal attacks between Russia and Ukraine.

item.title: Taliban Fighter Claims Killing 14 People in Panjshir Province
item.description: A Taliban fighter told a British tourist he personally killed 14 people in Panjshir province. The fighter, interviewed by YouTuber Will Bailey, described killing those who do not accept Islam. He also discussed fighting ISIS, stating it was harder than battling US forces. The video has sparked reactions online.

item.title: Taliban Fighter Admits Killing 14 in Panjshir in One Day
item.description: A Taliban fighter told a foreign YouTuber he killed 14 people in Panjshir in a single day. The fighter, interviewed by British YouTuber Will Bailey, described killing those who reject Islam without emotion. He stated this incident involved killing members of the Afghan National Resistance Front. The video has drawn widespread criticism.

item.title: Kazakhstan Authorities Given One Week to Develop Road Improvement Plans
item.description: Kazakhstan's regional administrations have been given one week to approve three-year plans for improving local road quality. These plans must cover all stages, from identifying priority areas to construction, quality control, and maintenance. This directive follows criticism from President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev regarding the state of road infrastructure. Contractors will be responsible for fixing defects within the warranty period at their own expense.

item.title: Unemployment Worsens in Afghanistan Amidst Economic Hardship and Limited Job Prospects
item.description: Afghan citizens report increasing unemployment and dwindling job opportunities, particularly for youth and heads of households. Since the Taliban's takeover, private sector jobs have sharply declined, and government hiring favors those with Taliban ties or experience. This has pushed many towards migration, temporary, or low-paying work, exacerbating economic hardship and limiting young people's futures.

item.title: Taliban Associates Allegedly Continue Gold Mining in Badakhshan Amidst Suspension for Other Miners
item.description: Gold miners in Badakhshan report that official mining activities have been suspended for two months, freezing their investments and causing losses. They claim individuals with ties or who bribe the Taliban continue operations, often at night. Miners who invested heavily are unable to resume work or recoup costs, facing further potential losses from winter conditions.

item.title: Belgian minister defends Taliban talks on deporting Afghan offenders
item.description: Belgium's Migration Minister Anneleen Van Bossuyt defended government talks with the Taliban regarding the deportation of convicted Afghan asylum seekers. She clarified these negotiations do not signify support for the Taliban, emphasizing their aim is public safety, particularly for women and girls.

item.title: Ministry of Internal Affairs warns parents to supervise their children
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Internal Affairs concluded its "Pay Attention – Children" operation, identifying over 25,000 minors unaccompanied at night. The ministry reported that nearly 3,000 directives were issued regarding road infrastructure near educational institutions, with over 40 officials held accountable for non-compliance.

item.title: Taliban Foreign Minister discusses new opportunities with UN Deputy Secretary-General
item.description: Taliban Foreign Minister Amir Khan Muttaqi met with UN Deputy Secretary-General Rosemary DiCarlo in Kabul to discuss finding new opportunities within the Doha Process. Discussions covered cooperation, humanitarian aid, migrant needs, climate change, and water issues, emphasizing practical outcomes and balanced reporting on Afghanistan.

item.title: Pakistan Violence Surges 83% in Q3 2026, Highest Since 2021
item.description: Pakistan experienced its sharpest rise in violence since 2021 during the third quarter of 2026, with over 1,400 deaths reported. The Center for Research and Security Studies noted an 83% increase in fatalities compared to the previous quarter, primarily in Balochistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa provinces.

item.title: Uzbekistan Increases Imports of Propane, Cars, and Electronics
item.description: Uzbekistan has significantly boosted its imports of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG), automobiles, and electronics. LPG imports alone reached $124 million, a 3.5-fold increase compared to the same period last year, indicating a growing demand for these goods.

item.title: Taliban Seek Russian Medicines After Pakistan Drug Import Ban
item.description: Afghanistan's Taliban health minister requested medicines, vaccines, and medical equipment from Russia, following a year-long ban on drug imports from Pakistan. The minister sought Russian assistance to improve health services and train specialists, with Moscow expressing readiness for technical cooperation.

item.title: Over 52 kg of Narcotics Seized in Surxondaryo Region, Uzbekistan
item.description: Authorities in Uzbekistan's Surxondaryo region intercepted over 52 kilograms of narcotics being smuggled from Afghanistan. During the inspection of a truck, 98 packages containing the drugs were discovered. The seized substances amount to nearly 340,000 doses.

item.title: Almaty Water Utility Denies Reports of Privatization
item.description: The state-owned enterprise "Almaty Su" has refuted information circulating in some media and social networks regarding the transfer of the city's water supply and sanitation system to a third-party company. The company stated that it continues to operate normally and that no transfer of management is planned. This information about handing over the city's water infrastructure to an external company is false.

item.title: Suspect Arrested in Aktau for Extortion Charges
item.description: Police in the Mangystau region, in cooperation with other law enforcement agencies, have arrested a suspect in an extortion case in Aktau. The individual allegedly demanded 300,000 tenge from a resident, threatening to release damaging information. The suspect was apprehended while receiving a portion of the demanded money and is currently in pre-trial detention.

item.title: Police find 25,000 unaccompanied children at night in Kazakhstan
item.description: Kazakh police identified over 25,000 minors unaccompanied by adults during nighttime hours as part of the 'Attention – Children!' operation. The Ministry of Internal Affairs urged parents to increase supervision of their children's whereabouts and activities, emphasizing parental responsibility for improper care.

item.title: Gold Mine Collapse in Takhar Kills Five Workers
item.description: Taliban local officials in Takhar province confirmed five workers died when a gold mine collapsed in the Shah-e-Mastan valley of Chah-Ab district. Details on the timing of the incident were not provided. This follows a similar incident last week where ten workers were rescued after being trapped.

item.title: Astana to Become Regional Hub for Humanoid and Robot Dog Production
item.description: Astana plans to establish a regional hub for producing humanoid robots, service robots, and robot dogs. This initiative stems from a strategic agreement with China's Unitree, signed during President Tokayev's visit to Shanghai. The project aims to create a new robotics industry in Kazakhstan.

item.title: Three Kazakh Startups to Visit Silicon Valley After Draper Founders Challenge
item.description: Three Kazakh tech startups have earned the opportunity to send representatives to Silicon Valley following the Draper Founders Challenge, held during the AI & Digital Bridge 2026 forum in Astana. BEST Vision will participate in Draper University's Hero Training program, while ARLAN BIOTECH, Cortex AI, and HubTalk AI will attend a two-week program.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Natural Gas Production Decreased by 16% in First 8 Months
item.description: Natural gas production in Uzbekistan fell by 16% during the first eight months of the year. Crude oil extraction also saw a decline, dropping from 434.5 thousand tons in the same period of 2025 to 425 thousand tons in 2026.

item.title: Russian Embassy in Kabul Expresses Concern Over Clashes Between Taliban and Pakistan
item.description: The Russian Embassy in Kabul has expressed concern over the ongoing military conflict between Pakistan and Afghanistan, citing recent airstrikes on Kunar and Helmand provinces. The embassy highlighted the impact on civilians, including children, following Pakistani airstrikes on October 1st.

item.title: Kazakh Sailor Demobilized After Surviving Caspian Tragedy
item.description: Akzhol Temerkhan, a sailor who survived a tragic incident on the Caspian Sea, has completed his mandatory military service. He was the sole conscript from Mangystau region to survive the incident. President Tokayev previously awarded him and two other survivors medals for courage. Temerkhan plans to visit families of fallen comrades.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Japan Discuss New Phase of JDS Program Focusing on AI and Smart Cities
item.description: Uzbekistan and Japan are advancing their cooperation through the JDS program, focusing on human capital development and modern governance. A meeting between Uzbekistan's Agency for Management of State Assets and Japan's JICE discussed enhancing the JDS program for 2027-2028. Priorities include AI, smart cities, climate change, and seismic risk management.

item.title: Kazakhstan Hosts AI & Digital Bridge 2026 Forum, Signing Key Agreements
item.description: Astana hosted the international technology forum AI & Digital Bridge 2026, focusing on artificial intelligence and digital technologies. The event facilitated the signing of memorandums and agreements between government bodies, tech companies, financial institutions, and international partners. These agreements aim to launch joint projects, attract investment, and foster technological exchange.

item.title: Personal Data of Over 520 Education Workers Illegally Published Online in Kyzylorda
item.description: The personal data of 529 education workers from seven organizations in the Kyzylorda region were illegally posted on the state procurement portal. The data appeared in documents related to medical examination services. Prosecutors intervened, removed the documents, and disciplined the responsible managers.

item.title: Afghan Chamber Delegation Attends Turkmenistan Investment Forum in Ashgabat
item.description: A delegation from the Afghanistan Chamber of Commerce and Investment (ACCI) attended the Third Turkmenistan Investment Forum in Ashgabat. Participants discussed investment opportunities and economic cooperation. The ACCI delegation presented Afghanistan's economic potential and invited the Turkmenistan Chamber of Commerce to visit Afghanistan.

item.title: Survivor of Caspian Tragedy Completes Military Service
item.description: A sailor who survived a tragic incident in the Caspian Sea has completed his mandatory military service. Akzhol Temerkhan, the sole survivor from his unit during a naval exercise that resulted in multiple fatalities, finished his service in the Kazakhstani Naval Forces. He plans to visit the families of his fallen comrades.

item.title: Almaty youth plant 2,000 saplings in Kok-Zhaiylau
item.description: Almaty youth and students participated in an ecological event in Kok-Zhaiylau, planting approximately 2,000 Schrenk spruce saplings. The initiative, supported by the Minister of Ecology and the city mayor, aims to foster environmental awareness and youth engagement in nature conservation.

item.title: Tokayev dismisses three from Kazakhstan's Defense Ministry
item.description: President Tokayev has dismissed three officials from Kazakhstan's Defense Ministry, including the Chief of the General Staff and deputy ministers. This action follows the deaths of 14 servicemen in the Caspian Sea, prompting a reshuffling of key military leadership.

item.title: US and Ukraine Sign First Mineral Extraction Deal, Valued at $70 Million
item.description: The US and Ukraine have finalized their first mineral extraction deal through an investment fund. The fund, established by a resource agreement, aims for projects potentially worth $70 million. An initial $30 million will target joint development with BGV Group in Ukraine, focusing on critical minerals like rare earths and uranium. Other projects support Ukraine's energy infrastructure.

item.title: Latvia Considers Suspending Visas for Uzbek Citizens Amid Crime Concerns
item.description: Latvia's Interior Ministry has proposed temporarily suspending visa issuance for Uzbek citizens, citing alleged crimes committed by individuals after arrival, including against minors. The ministry seeks to use this period for enhanced information exchange and checks with Uzbekistan. Lithuania previously halted work visa applications from Central Asian countries due to a surge in applications.

item.title: Kazakhstan Presents Botai Culture Heritage at Cambridge University Conference
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ambassador to the UK, Alibek Bakaev, spoke at a conference at Cambridge University's McDonald Institute for Archaeological Research. The event focused on ancient Eurasian interactions. The ambassador highlighted the importance of studying the Great Steppe's history and fostering international academic cooperation. A related exhibition, "Botai - Culture of the Great Steppe," was also opened.

item.title: Kazakhstan Issues Storm Warnings for All 17 Regions Amid Forecasted Severe Weather
item.description: Kazakhstan's meteorological service has issued storm warnings for all 17 regions, including Shymkent and mountainous areas of Almaty, for October 4th. Forecasts predict rain, snow, thunderstorms, hail, and strong winds across the country. Several regions face a high risk of fire danger due to dry conditions.

item.title: Uzbek President's daughter met with Donald Trump, details undisclosed
item.description: Saida Mirziyoyeva, daughter of Uzbekistan's president and head of the presidential administration, announced meeting with US President Donald Trump, sharing a photo on social media. She conveyed her father's best wishes to Trump. The White House has not commented on the meeting, which occurred ahead of a planned visit by US officials to Samarkand.

item.title: Sultan of Oman to make first-ever state visit to Kazakhstan
item.description: The Sultan of Oman, Haitham bin Tarik, will arrive in Astana on October 3 for a state visit, marking the first visit by an Omani head of state to Kazakhstan and Central Asia. Discussions with Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev will focus on new areas of cooperation, with several agreements expected to be signed.

item.title: Taliban Seek Russian Cooperation to Enhance Healthcare Services in Afghanistan
item.description: Afghanistan's acting public health minister, Noor Jalal Jalali, requested increased Russian cooperation to improve healthcare quality. During a meeting with Russia's health minister, Mikhail Albertovich Murashko, discussions focused on long-term health cooperation, including imports of medicines, vaccines, and medical equipment. Russia expressed readiness to expand technical cooperation in the health sector.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Establish AI, Energy, and Data Storage Research Centers with China
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to create three joint R&D centers focused on artificial intelligence, renewable energy, and data storage in collaboration with Chinese partners. These centers, to be based at Al-Farabi Kazakh National University, aim to foster research, adopt foreign technologies, and train specialists. The Ministry of Energy will coordinate these energy-related projects.

item.title: Personal Data of 529 Education Workers in Kyzylorda Region Leaked Online
item.description: The personal data of 529 education workers from the Kyzylorda region has been leaked and appeared online. The extent of the data breach and the specific information compromised have not been fully detailed.
